ON THE 16 th OF APRIL, 2024  CRIMINAL REVISION No. 5261 of 2023  BETWEEN:-
 SMT. JAYSHREE UPADHYAY W/O SHRI DINESH KUMAR  UPADHYAY, AGED ABOUT 52 YEARS, OCCUPATION:
 HOUSEWIFE R/O 409 TILAK NAGAR COLONY NO. 10  INDORE (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (BY SHRI PRATEEK MAHESHWARI, ADVOCATE)
 AND  DINESH KUMAR UPADHYAY S/O SHRI BADRILAL  UPADHYAY, AGED ABOUT 53 YEARS, OCCUPATION:
 GOVT. OFFICER R/O 25, SAJJAN VIHAR TILAK NAGAR  JAORA DISTT. RATLAM (MADHYA PRADESH)
 
 (MS. KIRTEE AGRAWAL, ADVOCATE.)
 This revision coming on for admission this day, th e co  following:

ORDER This revision petition u/S 19(4) of the Family Courts Act r/w section 397 of Cr.P.C. has been filed by the petitioner/wife being aggrieved by the order dated 27/07/2023 passed by IIIrd Additional Principal Judge, Family Court Indore in MJC no.709/ 2022, whereby the learned trial court has rejected an Interim maintenance application filed by the petitioner.

sentences.text: 2. It is admitted fact that the petitioner/ wife and respondent/ husband got married on 17/05/1993 as per Hindu rites and rituals.
One daughter named Riya was born from their wedlock and she is married.
It is also admitted fact that the respondent/ husband is working under Madhya Pradesh Health Department, and he received Rs.55,000/- per month as salary from there.

sentences.text: The petitioner/ wife has filed an application for maintenance u/S 125 of Cr.P.C. and has also filed an application for interim maintenance stating that after marriage, she used to live with respondent/ husband at her matrimonial house.
Thereafter, her husband started to harass her physically and mentally, in furtherance of demand of dowry and other domestic reasons.
It is also stated that the respondent has solemnized second marriage with a woman named Kalpana and has 2 children from their wedlock.
In year 2000, the respondent had deserted petitioner/ wife.
Since then she has been living at her maternal house.
The petitioner has no source of income to maintain herself.

While the respondent is in a government job and receives salary of more than Rs.55,000/-
per month.
Therefore, the respondent is capable to maintain the petitioner but he denied to maintain her.
She sought interim maintenance of Rs.50,000/- per month and counsel's fees Rs.25,000/- in lump sum.

4. The respondent/ husband in his reply has denied all the averments made in interim maintenance application, except admitted facts and pleaded that after marriage, the behaviour of petitioner/ wife was not fair with respondent/ husband and his family members.
She used to argue for trivial domestic causes and did not use to perform house chores.
She used to wake up late.

For a long time,
the respondent/ husband tolerated the behaviour of petitioner/ wife for a long time and despite of exhorting her for several times, she did not bring any improvement in her behaviour.
The respondent/ husband had filed a divorce petition u/S 13 of Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, wherein on 21/11/1994, on basis of compromise application, the matter was disposed of.
The petitioner/ wife even after agreeing in the compromise agreement, did not come back to live with husband at her matrimonial house.
The petitioner/ wife without any justified cause has been living separate from respondent/ husband.
After 27 years of living separately, the petitioner/ wife frivolously filed an FIR against respondent/ husband u/S 498A of IPC to pressurize him.

The petitioner has degree in M.A.
and B.Ed.
She lives as sole heir at her aunt Smt. Ramkunwar Bai's house at Indore.
She receives rent from the house as well.
She is capable to maintain herself.
The respondent/ husband and his mother has lots of regular health expenses and that is a major portion of his salary.
He has taken loan for education of his daughter.
The respondent is not able to maintain the petitioner.

Therefore,
application for interim maintenance is liable to be rejected.
5. The learned trial court after hearing both the parties, was prima facie of the view that the petitioner is living separate from the respondent without any reason.
She has not fulfilled her matrimonial duties.
During 2014 - 2018, when the respondent was suffering from serious disease i.e. lungs infection, she did not take care of him.
It has not been explained by her that from last 20 years, how had she managed to maintain herself.
The petitioner is able to maintain herself.
Therefore, the learned trial court has rejected the interim maintenance application as stated above.
6. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that, the impugned order is against law, incorrect and perverse.
Therefore, it deserves to be set aside.
It is also submitted that the learned trial court has not considered facts which was admitted by the respondent.
It is also submitted that the learned trial Court has wrongly rejected the application on the basis of those facts which were required to be proved after adducing of evidence by the parties.

It is also submitted that the learned trial court has committed error in considering that the maintenance application has been filed belatedly and how the petitioner has maintained herself meanwhile has not been explained.

The learned counsel has Smt. Jayshree Upadhyay vs Dinesh Kumar Upadhyay on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103103653/
2 placed reliance on the case of, Chandrakant Jain Vs. Veer Mati Jain [2020 SCCOnline Raj 1772].
7.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer of the petitioner and supported the impugned order.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the records.

9. In the case of Chandrakant Jain (Supra), the Rajasthan High Court has opined as under in paragraph 5:-
"5.

In the opinion of this Court, an order under section 125 of Cr.P.C. is in the nature of interim maintenance and husband, who admittedly earns Rs.40,000/- per month cannot be absolved of his obligation to pay interim maintenance, merely because the respondent-wife has chosen to file the application after 36 years of marriage."

10. It is clear that, interim maintenance cannot be denied merely on the basis that the application has been filed after a long period by putting on a question that how had the applicant managed to maintain herself meanwhile.

11. In the case of Chandar Kaushal Vs. Mrs. Veena Kaushal [(1978) 4 SCC 70] following observation is given:-
"9. This provision is a measure of social justice and specially enacted to protect women and children and falls within the constitutional sweep of Article 15(3)
reinforced by Article 39.

entities.text: Chandar Kaushal Vs. Mrs. Veena Kaushal [(1978) 4 SCC 70]
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: We have no doubt that sections of statutes calling for construction by courts are not petrified print but vibrant words with social functions to fulfil.
The brooding presence of the constitutional empathy for the weaker sections like women and children must inform interpretation if it has to have social relevance.

So viewed, it is possible to be selective in picking out that interpretation out of two alternatives which advance the cause -- the cause of the derelicts."
12.

In pursuance of guideline given by the Apex court in the case of Rajnesh Vs. Neha [CRA no. 930/
2020], both the parties have filed affidavit to show their asset and liabilities.
It is revealed from the affidavit of the petitioner that she has no source of income and neither she has any liability.
The respondent has shown his salary to be Rs.54,000/- per month.
He has also shown his liability in his affidavit.
But it appears that he has not filed document alongwith affidavit before the trial court as he has mentioned in paragraph () 5(a),(b),(c) and 7 of affidavit that he will file it later.
The affidavits filed by the respondent/ husband is not in accordance with the guideline given by the Apex court in Rajnesh Case (Supra).
It appears that the learned trial court has also not drawn its attention towards affidavit filed by the respondent/ husband.
It also appears that the trial court has not considered the aforementioned affidavits in the impugned order at all.
13. In the instant case prima facie undisputedly the respondent is in a government job and he gets salary of Rs.55,000/- per month.
Admittedly, the petitioner is a married wife of the respondent and Smt. Jayshree Upadhyay vs Dinesh Kumar Upadhyay on 16 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/103103653/

sentences.text: 3 she is living separately from her husband/ respondent for a long time.
It can be decided on the merits that the petitioner has sufficient reason to live separate from respondent/ husband or not.
There is no prima facie material to show that the petitioner has capacity to maintain herself, and the same can be decided on the basis of evidence.
Therefore, it is clear that the learned trial court has committed error by rejecting the interim maintenance application of the petitioner.
14. Resultantly, impugned order dated 27/07/2023 is hereby set aside.

Revision petition filed by the petitioner is allowed and looking to the facts and circumstances of the case also considering monthly income and liability of the respondent, he is directed to pay Rs.5,000/- per month interim maintenance to the petitioner from the date of filing of maintenance application.
